title: Grammar: Narrative Tenses — Past Simple, Past Continuous, Past Perfect
grammarTip:
Три времени в нарративном письме работают вместе:

Past Simple → основные события в хронологическом порядке:
"She arrived, sat down, and opened her notebook."

Past Continuous → фоновые действия, атмосфера:
"The sun was setting. Students were leaving the library."

Past Perfect → действие ДО основного события:
"She had already read the report before the meeting started."

💡 Комбинируй все три для живого, профессионального нарратива:
"When she arrived, the meeting had already started. The professor was explaining something complex. She sat down quietly."

grammarTable.subject: Past Simple
grammarTable.example: She opened the door. He said nothing. They left.

grammarTable.subject: Past Continuous
grammarTable.example: The rain was falling. People were walking past.

grammarTable.subject: Past Perfect

grammarTable.subject: Past Perf. Cont.
grammarTable.example: She had been waiting for years. He had been living alone.

grammarTable.subject: Sequence

rows.example: She walked in, sat down, and opened her notebook.

rows.form: Specific past events (with or without time reference)
rows.example: He called her three times. She never answered.
"I can't stay," she said. He nodded and looked away.
The lights were flickering. Children were running outside.

rows.form: Action in progress when main event occurs
rows.example: He was crossing the bridge when he saw her.
She was cooking while he was reading.
She had lived there for twenty years before leaving.
He was nervous because he had failed once before.

rows.form: Switch to past perfect, then back to past simple
rows.example: She had grown up here. Now she was returning. (back to past simple)

rows.form: Sequence: as soon as, the moment, immediately after
rows.example: As soon as she saw him, she turned away.

rows.form: Simultaneity: while, as, at the same time as
rows.example: While she was talking, he was watching her carefully.

rows.form: Just before/after: just as, no sooner … than, by the time
rows.example: No sooner had she sat down than the lights went out.

rows.form: Earlier event: before, already, by then, previously
rows.example: By the time he arrived, she had already left.

rows.form: ❌ Tense slip: present tense in a past narrative
rows.example: ✅ She opened the door. ❌ She opens the door.
✅ Use it once to establish the earlier event, then return to past simple.
✅ The rain WAS FALLING (cont.), not "the rain fell" (for ongoing background).
✅ She WAS WALKING when the phone RANG — not "she walked when the phone rang."

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct tense for the main action.
Choose the correct tense for the background.
exercises.text: "___ (snow / fall) outside, and the streets ___ (be) empty."
"He ___ (live) in that house for ten years before he finally moved out." (Earlier event)
exercises.hint: Past perfect = event/state before the narrative present
Past continuous + when + past simple = interrupted action

exercises.text: "No sooner ___ she ___ (sit down) than the lights went out."
exercises.hint: No sooner had + subject + pp... than = immediate sequence

exercises.instruction: Which sentence correctly establishes backstory and returns to past simple?
opts: She had grown up here. She had felt out of place. She had decided to leave.
She had grown up here. She felt out of place. She decided to leave.
She grew up here. She felt out of place. She decided to leave.
She was growing up here. She felt out of place. She decided to leave.
exercises.correct: She had grown up here. She felt out of place. She decided to leave.
exercises.hint: One past perfect to establish, then return to past simple

exercises.text: "By the time the ambulance ___ (arrive), he ___ (already / lose) consciousness."
exercises.hint: "By the time" + past simple; earlier event = past perfect

exercises.text: "The music plays softly as she enters the room."
exercises.hint: Present tense in a past narrative = tense inconsistency error

exercises.text: "___ she saw the letter, she knew something had gone wrong."
exercises.hint: "As soon as" = the moment she saw it

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the past perfect continuous.
exercises.text: "She looked exhausted. She ___ (wait) for over three hours."
exercises.hint: Past perfect continuous = ongoing action before the narrative moment

exercises.instruction: Which uses the past continuous correctly?
opts: The children were played in the garden.
The children playing in the garden.
The children were playing in the garden when the storm began.
The children had been played in the garden.
exercises.correct: The children were playing in the garden when the storm began.
exercises.hint: Past continuous + when + past simple = interrupted scene

exercises.text: "While she ___ (cook), he ___ (sit) at the window and watch the rain."
exercises.hint: While + past continuous; simultaneous main action = past simple

opts: She noticed every detail of the room.
Her hands were trembling as she opened the envelope.
He said her name once, quietly.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct narrative tense.
exercises.text: "He ___ (stand) in the doorway. The house ___ (smell) of old books. Nothing ___ (change) since he ___ (leave)."
exercises.correct: stood / smelled / had changed / had left

opts: Just as she reached the door, she was hearing her name.
Just as she reached the door, she heard her name.
Just as she had reached the door, she heard her name.
Just as she reaches the door, she heard her name.
exercises.correct: Just as she reached the door, she heard her name.
exercises.hint: "Just as" + past simple + past simple = simultaneous events

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses past perfect correctly for motivation?
opts: She was nervous. She will fail before.
She was nervous because she failed before.
She was nervous because she had failed before.
She was nervous because she was failing before.
exercises.correct: She was nervous because she had failed before.
exercises.hint: Past perfect = earlier event that explains current state

questions.text: "___ (music/play) softly and the candles ___ (flicker) on the table." (Scene-setting)
"She ___ across the room when the stranger ___ her name." Choose the correct forms.
"He ___ (never / be) to that part of the city before that evening."
questions.hint: Past perfect = event/state before the narrative moment

questions.text: "No sooner ___ she ___ (open) the door than she heard footsteps."
Which correctly uses the past perfect for backstory?
opts: She lived there for ten years.
She was living there for ten years.
She had lived there for ten years.
She lives there for ten years.
questions.correct: She had lived there for ten years.
questions.hint: Past perfect = state before the narrative present

questions.text: Once the past perfect establishes a backstory, you should continue using it for the whole passage.
questions.hint: Use it once, then return to past simple

questions.text: "By the time they ___ (arrive), the show ___ (already / start)."
questions.hint: "By the time" + past simple; earlier event = past perfect

questions.text: "While he was reading, she ___ quietly out of the room." Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: Main action in the "while" clause: past simple

questions.text: "She looked pale. She ___ (be) ill for days."
questions.hint: Past perfect = state going on before the current moment

opts: As she was walking, the rain was starting.
As she walked, the rain started.
She was walking when the rain started.
She walked when the rain was starting.
questions.correct: She was walking when the rain started.

questions.text: "She had been ___ (wait) for two hours by the time he finally appeared."
Which sentence has a tense consistency error?
opts: She opened the door. She stepped inside.
The lights were off. She felt her way to the wall.
He looks up. He had not expected her.
She had seen him before, but she could not remember where.
questions.correct: He looks up. He had not expected her.
questions.hint: "Looks" = present tense slip in a past narrative
